title: Emergency secret rotation during an incident (v1)
author: Grace O'Connor
body:
> **Archived 2024-07-18:** this page is superseded by "Emergency secret rotation during an incident" and is kept for reference only.

# Goal
Describe how to rotate secrets fast and in a coordinated way while an incident is active (suspected compromise, or containment requires it).

# Should we rotate now?
Rotate right away when any of these apply:
- credible evidence that a secret was exposed
- access patterns that look like key misuse
- a vendor reports compromised credentials
- an attacker can reach systems able to read secrets

For availability-only incidents with no compromise signal, use normal mitigation first; emergency rotation carries its own risk.

# Roles
- Security Lead: authorizes emergency rotation and decides which secrets go first
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates the response and keeps the timeline
- Ops/SRE: makes the changes and watches service health
- Service owners: update consumers and confirm things still work

# Procedure
1. Post in the incident channel: 'Emergency secret rotation in progress', listing candidate secrets by name/path only.
2. Link any break-glass event and confirm audit logging is enabled.
3. Order the work:
   - Tier 0 first (signing keys, privileged service tokens)
   - Tier 1 after (DB creds, message bus creds, broadly scoped third-party keys)
4. Per secret:
   - look up consumers in the service ownership spreadsheet
   - pick a rotation pattern (dual-valid where supported, otherwise cutover)
   - rotate the credential at the issuer
   - write the new value to Vault/secret store
   - restart or redeploy consumers as needed
   - check per-service health (auth failures, latency, error rate)
5. If failures persist beyond 20 minutes and customer impact keeps growing, stop and decide: roll back or keep rotating.
6. Note exact timestamps of the issuer-side change and each consumer rollout.

# Communications
- Never paste secret values into Slack, tickets, or docs.
- Where customers will notice, align messaging with Support.

# After-action requirements
- Confirm break-glass access has been revoked.
- Open a post-incident review item listing rotated secrets, affected services, and follow-up rotations (derived tokens, cached credentials).

This version of the procedure is deprecated; refer to the current page for the active process.
